blocks.content: Recognize major alteration definition and common avionics examples.

items.definition: A change to type design that might appreciably affect structural strength, flight characteristics, or other airworthiness qualities — and is not listed in the aircraft specifications or type certificate data sheet.
items.analogy: Like a structural renovation changing a building's load-bearing capacity — it needs engineering review and a permit, unlike replacing a light fixture.

items.term: STC + Flight Manual Supplement = Major Alteration
items.definition: An STC installation that includes a flight manual supplement is a major alteration — regardless of the part's TSO status — because it changes the aircraft's approved operating limitations or procedures.
items.analogy: A TSO on the part is like a UL listing on an appliance — the part is approved, but modifying your home's electrical panel to install it still requires a permit.

blocks.question: Per 14 CFR Part 43 Appendix A, how is a major alteration defined?
choices: Any repair costing more than $1,000 in parts and labor
Any alteration not specifically covered by the aircraft's POH
A change to type design that might appreciably affect structural strength, flight characteristics, or other airworthiness qualities
Any repair requiring an IA to approve the return-to-service
blocks.feedback: The regulatory definition focuses on the effect on airworthiness: a type design change that might appreciably affect structural strength, flight characteristics, or other airworthiness qualities. Cost, POH coverage, and IA involvement are not the determining factors.

blocks.question: A shop installs an avionics system under an STC. The STC data package includes a flight manual supplement changing VFR-only to IFR-approved operations. This installation should be classified as:
choices: A minor alteration — avionics do not affect structural strength
A major alteration — the flight manual supplement signals a change affecting airworthiness qualities
A line replacement — the part has a TSO so no alteration approval is needed
Preventive maintenance — pilots can perform STC installations on their own aircraft
blocks.feedback: The flight manual supplement signals the change affects aircraft airworthiness qualities (operating limitations). That meets the Part 43 Appendix A major alteration definition. TSO approval on the part does not determine the classification of the installation.
